title: Stadium grant, climate target and intimate partner violence
subtitle: Beechwood West levy, Generation Park funding, security contract, Albert Street rezoning and redevelopment planning briefing
overview: Council approved a one-time $2.5 million capital grant to Wilfrid Laurier University for its stadium improvement project {{vote:m4}}. The City is to receive community access to the upgraded field, to be allocated under the City's own policies. Council also tightened its corporate climate goal to net zero by 2050, matching the national target, and asked staff to report on the cost before the 2024-2026 budget is finalized {{vote:m5}}.

Council declared intimate partner violence an epidemic and asked the Province to do the same and to fund prevention {{vote:m9}}. It approved a special service area levy for the Beechwood West II Homes Association {{vote:m3}}, released $2 million for Generation Park {{vote:m6}}, and awarded a two-year security guard contract {{vote:m7}}. It also approved a zoning change for Albert Street and Batavia Place {{vote:m8}}.

Council also heard presentations from Reep Green Solutions and planning staff, and a proposed housing zoning motion was tabled for the October 30 meeting. Council met in closed session earlier in the afternoon. The minutes record no public decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved a one-time $2.5 million capital grant for the stadium improvement project, paid once a contribution agreement is signed and including community access terms.
Council amended the corporate greenhouse gas target to net zero by 2050, approved the plan direction, and asked staff to report on planning and budget effects before the 2024-2026 budget is approved.
Council declared intimate partner violence an epidemic, asked the Province to do likewise and fund prevention, and committed to keep supporting the Region's Community Safety and Well-being Plan.

decisions.item: Beechwood West II special service levy
decisions.detail: Council approved a special service area levy for properties in the association's area starting in 2024 and authorized the related licence, operating and lease agreements.
Council released $2,000,000 in 2023 capital funding for the West Side Employment Lands project from the Industrial Land Reserve Fund.
Council awarded RFP 23-15 to Barber-Collins Security Services Ltd. for a total of $1,244,709.70 over an initial two-year term.

decisions.item: Albert Street and Batavia Place zoning
decisions.detail: Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-06, removing the holding symbol from five properties on Batavia Place and Albert Street.

debate: On the stadium grant, councillors asked how community access would work. Staff said the City would allocate the community hours under its own affiliation policy, with prime-time hours negotiated, mostly in spring and summer. One councillor asked about the second phase, which the university's board had not yet approved. The university said the first phase's groundwork enables it, and the funding would be sequenced across the two phases.

On the climate target, one councillor supported aligning with the national target but was uneasy about adopting it before hearing staff's view on cost. Staff said the 2050 change does not affect the climate action plan itself. They had no itemized costs yet, noted that most corporate emissions come from facilities, and said the budget process would bring estimates. Staff also said property taxes and user fees alone would struggle to cover the cost.

On intimate partner violence, delegates from the Family Violence project cited rising police calls and charges and more severe injuries seen at hospitals. They said a declaration costs nothing and signals support to victims and service workers. One councillor backed the motion but wanted any provincial response to emphasize prevention and root causes over punitive measures. A delegate agreed and described work engaging men.

On Generation Park, a councillor asked about the long-delayed dog park, and staff said design would start this fall, with public consultation and construction in 2024 as weather permits. Councillors also raised parking, transit service and protected bike lanes for the employment area.

In the planning briefing, staff said master planning can produce better layouts and faster approvals on large redevelopment sites. One councillor asked what residents can expect and how they can have input, given limited consultation under Bill 23.
